newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's BHP stock melts away as copper prices sink.
newsitem.headline: Australia's BHP stock melts away as copper prices sink.

text.p: The stock of Broken Hill Pty Co. Ltd. sank to a two-year low Thursday as a plunge in copper prices sparked a sell-off this week that has wiped more than A$1.5 billion ($1.2 billion) from the company's market value.
The Australian steel, energy and minerals giant, the world's second-biggest producer of copper, was again battered on the Australian stock market as copper prices continued to fall.
BHP breached a previous 1996 low of A$15.90 ($12.72) and fell to A$15.58 ($12.46), its lowest level since May 1994, closing at A$16.00 ($12.80).
The drop reflected concern at the impact of weak copper and steel prices on BHP's earnings.

Copper prices, which averaged $1.15 a pound in the first half of 1996, were down 13 percent from a year ago and have since fallen to less than 90 cents so far in the second half. On Thursday, copper traded at 87.50 cents a pound on New York's Commodity Exchange.
